name: Amazon
foundedNote: Jeff Bezos filed articles of incorporation in Washington State on 1994-07-05 under the name Cadabra, Inc., and renamed it Amazon.com, Inc. within a few months after a lawyer misheard 'Cadabra' as 'cadaver'. The filings corroborate the month but not the day: the IPO prospectus says only 'The Company was incorporated in Washington in July 1994', and records Bezos buying 10,200,000 founder shares for $10,000 in July 1994. The 1994-07-05 date and the Cadabra name come from Wikipedia rather than from a filing. Amazon reincorporated in Delaware on 1996-05-28 through a Washington-into-Delaware merger (S-1 Exhibit 2.1, 'Agreement and Plan of Merger dated May 28, 1996'), five weeks before the Kleiner Perkins round; per the brief this chart clocks from the original Washington incorporation, so t=0 is 22 months before the Delaware entity existed.

annualOverrides.note: IPO day. 3,000,000 shares priced at $18.00; the final prospectus states 23,858,702 shares outstanding after the offering (as of 1997-05-13). The over-allotment was never exercised — the FY1997 10-K reports net proceeds of $49.1 million after ~$4.9 million of expenses, i.e. $54.0 million gross, exactly 3,000,000 x $18.00. The stock closed its first session at $23.50, which gives 23,858,702 x $23.50 = $560.7M and matches CNBC's '$560 million' to the dollar. At the $18.00 offer price the figure is $429M; the widely repeated '$438M' silently assumes the 450,000-share over-allotment that was not taken.

events.note: Below the inclusion floor — family money with no institutional lead and no disclosed valuation, so recorded but never plotted. The prospectus 'Certain Transactions' section itemises both legs at $0.1717 per share (split-adjusted): 582,528 shares to Miguel A. Bezos in February 1995 ($100,020) and 847,716 shares to the Gise Family Trust in July 1995 ($145,553). The two sum to $245,573, which is exactly the figure Wikipedia and every secondary account report for 'Bezos' parents' investment' — the S-1 shows it was two purchases five months apart, not one cheque. Dated here to the first leg.

events.nameConflict: Amazon's only pre-IPO preferred series. Secondary accounts usually call it just 'the Kleiner Perkins round'.
events.note: First round with a named institutional lead, and the only pre-IPO institutional round. Reconstructed from the legal cap table rather than from press: the prospectus records 555,161 shares to Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VIII and 14,235 to KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, both at $14.05 per share — 569,396 shares for $8,000,013.80. S-1 Exhibit 10.2, the Series A Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement dated June 21, 1996, gives the closing-day denominator in its section 2.2 capitalisation representation: 2,589,711 common shares issued and outstanding. Series A converted 1:1 at the time (6:1 after the November 1996 4-for-1 and April 1997 3-for-2 splits), so post-money on outstanding as-converted shares is (2,589,711 + 569,396) x $14.05 = $44.39M, pre-money $36.39M, and Kleiner's stake 18.0% — which the prospectus corroborates at 16.3% by May 1997 after a year of dilution. The widely repeated '$8M for 13% at a $60M valuation' (HistoryLink, following Brad Stone) cannot be reconciled with those share counts: 13% would require 4.38M shares outstanding when the signed agreement says 3.16M. Adding the 414,636 options then outstanding and the 341,615-share reserve gets to $55.0M fully diluted, which is the closest any defensible convention comes to $60M. Marked soft because the choice between the outstanding and fully-diluted convention moves the number 24%.

Below the inclusion floor and not plotted: a $200,000 purchase by two sitting directors, not a priced institutional round. The prospectus records 2,500 shares of Series A each to Scott D. Cook and Patricia Q. Stonesifer at $40.00 per share, and dates Stonesifer's purchase to February 1997. The price is 2.85x the $14.05 Kleiner paid eight months earlier; against the 20,798,782 as-converted shares outstanding at March 31, 1997 it implies roughly $139M, but that is an inference from a director's cheque rather than a negotiated round price, so no valuation is recorded.

curatorNotes: The 1997 prospectus is unusually generous: it itemises every private sale of stock since inception, and Exhibit 10.2 hands over the closing-day share count for the Kleiner round, so the pre-IPO history here rests almost entirely on filings rather than on recollection. Two things the S-1 shows that the shards do not carry as events. First, an angel syndicate: the statement of stockholders' equity shows 4,235,244 common shares sold during 1995 for $1,172,000, of which only 1,430,244 shares / $245,573 were the family purchases, leaving roughly 2.8M shares at $0.3333 — the ~$1M raised from about twenty angels that secondary accounts describe, including director Tom A. Alberg's 150,000 shares in December 1995. The per-share amounts do not reconcile to the thousands-rounded total, so no amount is asserted. Second, Amazon's stock split four times (1998-06-02 2:1, 1999-01-05 3:1, 1999-09-02 2:1, 2022-06-06 20:1); only the 2022 split falls inside the SEC share series the pipeline reads (2009+), and it is derived from the jump in cover-page counts rather than entered here. Note also that all share and per-share figures in the prospectus are retroactively adjusted for the November 23, 1996 4-for-1 and April 18, 1997 3-for-2 splits, which is why the Series A converts 6:1 there but 1:1 in the June 1996 purchase agreement. CNBC dates the Kleiner investment to 1995; the signed purchase agreement is dated June 21, 1996.
unresolved: The 1995-96 angel syndicate: the S-1 equity statement implies ~2.8M shares at $0.3333 beyond the family purchases, but the per-share arithmetic does not close against the rounded $1,172,000 total, and no filing names the investors.

Whether the widely cited '$8M for 13% at $60M' for the June 1996 round reflects some fully-diluted convention or is simply wrong. The signed purchase agreement's share counts support 18.0% and $44.4M outstanding, or $55.0M fully diluted; neither yields 13%.
The 1994-07-05 incorporation day and the Cadabra, Inc. name are not in any SEC filing — the prospectus says only 'July 1994'. Washington's corporate registry was not consulted.
